answer_1.quote: In this paper, we explore the impact of input representations in data-to-text generation, i.e. in tasks where the input of an NLG system is structured data and the output is coherent and contextually relevant natural language texts.
answer_1.outputs: coherent and contextually relevant natural language texts

answer_2.quote: We use reference-based automated metrics primarily to assess the degree to which our seq2seq model learns to match the kinds of texts present in the corpora, though we also report the LLMs' performance for reference.

answer_4.quote: We recruited 36 participants for each dataset through Prolific.
answer_4.guideline: For fluency, we adapted the questions used by WebNLG 2023, asking participants to 'rate the Output in terms of Fluency' and explaining that [h]ighly fluent text 'flows well' and is well-connected and free from disfluencies'. For semantic fidelity (i.e. the faithfulness of the outputs to the inputs), participants saw a table of subjects, predicates, and objects meant to be present in the Output and had to click a radio button to indicate whether that element of the meaning was present, missing, or incorrect.
